#3824. Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

There's a lot of demand right now for a PC version of GTA 6. I'd love a proper PC port of The Warriors, first, and not just because I like coming up with fancy ways to talk about Ferris wheels. A PC port would be a timely reminder that Rockstar used to make city games that aren't open worlds, city games made of levels, and were pretty good at it. The classic thrill of GTA is to jump into a car and circle the metropolis, radio on and arm dangling, snatches of pedestrian dialogue bursting in your wake as you zip through downtown, the skyscrapers streaming by and evaporating, the world your oyster. In The Warriors, the city is No Man's Land and the night is a tightly compartmentalised maze. Your goal is to reach the other side of it on your own two feet, before a thousand rival miscreants kick your head in.

You lead a group of angry young guys of different ethnicities, wearing tribal colours and following a martial code - spiritual descendants of the stranded Greek soldiers of Xenephon's Anabais. Women barely feature in this relentlessly macho fable, and are mostly depicted as victims or seducers. Other genders are totally absent, while gay characters were considered for the film, but eventually cut. The game expands the storyline, filling in events before the titular Coney Island tearaways find themselves framed for a murder during an attempted city-wide gang uprising. But it otherwise adheres religiously to the movie's dingy and hyperbolic direction, hugging the visual language in ways that are slightly odd to return to, now that Rockstar have arguably outgrown their nerdy inferiority complex before the giants of cinema.

The game's New York is mysterious and sparsely populated: the only people abroad are other gangs and cops. The playable areas eschew affluent districts and pleasure zones; instead, you hop over a million chainlink fences in subway terminals and trashy alleyways. Most of the buildings are sealed and silent. The sky is a painted forest of chimneys, silos and stripped low cloud. You keep waiting for Batman to descend from the girders of a flyover; some of the enemy gangs certainly wouldn't look out of place in Rocksteady's Arkham. The murk isn't quite as pungent as you'd find in a PS1 flâneur like Urban Chaos, but it's respectably enveloping. I'd linger here, a plummy-accented tourist with a headful of references, cooing decorously over the stained and withdrawn shopfronts, were it not for the constant risk of getting stomped.

Back in the day, a few reviewers described The Warriors as having "deep" combat, offering a selection of directional jabs and kicks, grappling moves, terrain finishers and squad commands. I can't really see it. Certainly, The Warriors is no Sleeping Dogs. What the Warriors is is a believably chaotic brawler, with an enjoyable taste for friendly fire.

You spot a couple other Warriors surrounded by face-painted Baseball Furies, and launch into a crossbody tackle that bowls the whole group over. You straddle one of the clowns and are about to punch his teeth out when a friend lobs a trash can at the both of you. Now black-eyed and bleeding, you seize a dropped bat and swing randomly into the mob of warring outfits. Insults, taunts, chair legs and beer bottles fly back and forth. It feels like a fight. The riot spills out over each map, onto rooftops and into any businesses that have unwisely decided to stay open late. Looking back, I can see the first inklings of those spectacular drunken bar scuffles in Red Dead Redemption 2, though nobody's packing heat. The almost total absence of guns is, of course, the other thing that makes The Warriors novel, if you come to it from GTA.

I've yet to play Rockstar's latest GTA, which is now available on console worldwide. I've yet to decide how it fits into my evolving half-arsed anthropology of videogame nightlife. Still, I've spent a fair amount of time looking at screenshots and videos, and I'm finding the nights too bright. Too bright! All those shades seeping everywhere, all those rays being traced, all the spotlights and sequins, the way everything glimmers or glistens – it's too heady for me. Send me back to 2005's New York, where the darkness feels like it's part of the very mortar, and there's always a friend willing to "accidentally" hurl a bin at my head.

#3823. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

Mysterious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reemerged in the wake of GTA 6's release with another leak: This time, they have released what they claim to be a near-complete build of GTA 6 on Xbox from November 2026.

#3821. Fish with a sniper rifle takes aim at Tim Sweeney's hopes and dreams, as genAI-free meme game tops Epic Games' vibe-coding megajam

Epic Games are, as you're probably aware, going big on genAI at the moment. To the extent that, last month, the Tim Sweeney-helmed company announced the Epic AI MegaJam. Build a playable game in Unreal Engine or Unreal Editor for Fortnite with help from as many AI agents or tools as you like was the pitch.

So, naturally, sorting the submissions by 'Popular' turns up a game about a fish with a sniper rifle whose creator says they deliberately made it without using any generative AI.

The game's called LSD:FIH and sees a cigarette-smoking bit of shoe-wearing marine life go full MLG and start pulling off trickshots on blobs. If you struggled to parse that, you'll probably struggle even more with developer PolyCube's description of it as being a "computer game about a fih aura-farming". "No AI was used to make this game," is the other line in their description, which is far easier to parse.

"I made a game for the Epic's 'vibe-coding gamejam' megajam without using any AI in four days," they expanded on not Bluesky. "Sorta ran out of time so gameplay didn't turn out how I wanted, but hey it's still pretty aura."

Other submissions the megajam included a game called THIS GAME IS AI SLOP and one dubbed Goon Patrol - Director's Cut. If you're wondering how a game without genAI use could be allowed to stand among the slop masterpieces, it's because Epic ended up having to make clearer not long after the jam was announced that submissions didn't have to make use of genAI as a hard rule, leaving it up to the developer how much or little was worked in.

Still, I imagine noted genAI advocate Tim Sweeney's not best pleased that a game deliberately swimming against the slop tide shows up at the top if you hit up the Popular filter. Then again, he's been very busy posting important things about the situation with Jensen Huang and Nvidia lately, so maybe he hasn't noticed.

Yes, the last post I've linked there is the Sweens giggling at an AI image of him, Huang, Johan Andersson, and John Carmack as the heads carved into Mount Rushmore that he himself asked Grok to generate. As you do.

Rockstar apparently gave in to his demands

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Lawrence Sullivan, better known online as the 'Florida Joker,' has confirmed that he voices his lookalike in GTA 6. His character appears in an in-game viral social media video that shows his purple-haired homage confronting another man for stealing his look, knocking him out, and later being arrested.

Florida Joker, so called for his distinctive face tattoos and bright hair color, went viral after people spotted his mug shot online. His image apparently caught the eyes of people at Rockstar, as a similar-looking character appeared in the announcement trailer for GTA 6. Rockstar never confirmed that the purple-haired person was based on Sullivan, but the tattoos bore more than a few similarities to Sullivan's.

Rockstar actually hired Florida Joker to play his character in GTA 6, and he’s included in the credits. He’s part of the local population in the game and can be seen fighting another NPC in a social media clip, which led to his arrest. https://t.co/vCEifONSRMNovember 20, 2026

Sullivan originally claimed that he was going to sue Rockstar for $10 million over the apparent use of his likeness, but soon dropped his demands down to involvement in the game. "Let me voice the character. Let me go to the meet-and-greets. Let me promote the game," he says.

It appears Sullivan got his way, as he has now announced his involvement in GTA 6 in a video on social media where he says, "What's up? It's your boy Florida Joker, official voice actor on the GTA 6 game. For the last three years a lot of people were saying that I was not going to be in the game… but now it's time for me to s*** on them."

You can find Sullivan's name in the credits alongside the other voice actors for the game's 'local population.' His character appears in a Snapmatic clip where he gets in a fight with another local. After knocking the other guy out, you can hear Sullivan say, "Who the real one now b****. Take them fake tats off."

Seems that sometimes you can always get what you want.

While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park.

It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6.

As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update.

If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. If you save in first-person then immediately load the same save you'll be back in third-person and have to return to God's own preferred viewpoint.

#3817. Ubisoft lay off 166 more staff, this time at their Montreal and Quebec City studios, while mumbling about "current production priorities and business needs"

"Our production needs are changing," publishers claim

Ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the company.

Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft said in a statement handed to both sites. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources."

Ubisoft Montreal are currently working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, reportedly a witchy tale set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire, which switched creative directors earlier this ear and is one of the games Ubi are keen to get out of the door. What Quebec have been up to since Shadows shipped is less clear. They're a much smaller than Montreal and were founded in 2005.

Ubisoft have been carrying out mass cuts across their studios worldwide all the way through this year. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx. Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona. Long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm. Ubisoft's Paris HQ. Three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz. All have been subjected to some form of cuts or closure.

Meanwhile. changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Solidarity to all of the Ubisoft workers who've been affected by these layoffs in Montreal and Quebec.

#3816. It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the big release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either."

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe."

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

GTA 6 credits actually include 'Florida Joker', the viral internet personality who once demanded $10 million from Rockstar Games

#3814. Ignore that other game about crime that's out and burgle some ugly farmhouses in Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" with a 2000s Cartoon Network vibe

Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be important or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere."

With the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are."

Keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

Each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an important thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

Rockstar's hoping to innovate with Vice City's newest iteration

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Quote of the Day is a member-exclusive column here on GamesRadar+. Every day, we'll bring you a new talking point drawn from major industry interviews or our historic magazine archive. To get access to the entire collection, you can simply sign up to our free membership program below.

If you're anything like me, you're planning on settling down to a long weekend of GTA 6. But before you do, it might be worth hearing from Rockstar VP of design, Stephen Donkin, who says that Vice City represents a new kind of open world - one you shouldn't try and approach in the same way as a traditional game.

"There is so much to do in Leonida," Donkin said in development notes supplied to press. "And so much to discover, that we hope players get to the point where they stop thinking in tasks, completion percentages, online guides, and rather let the game unfold in front of them."

It's a bold ambition for players trained on at least a generation of games that do ask them to approach open worlds like a checklist, but Donkin has his reasons: "When you play the game and take your time with it, playing at the pace it asks you to, it can really unfold in front of you in a way that can feel almost infinite at a macro level, but each individual encounter still feels hand-crafted and with a human behind it," he says. "If players can let go and submit to becoming immersed in the world of Leonida, and just follow their nose as they play, they will feel the Leonida I have felt - and that's all we could ask for."

This is actually one of the things that's making me most excited to experience GTA 6. The depth of some of its systems make it sound more like an RPG or even an immersive sim than the traditional action games that the previous games in the series have been, and getting a chance to invest in those slowly strikes me as the thing that's likely to set GTA 6 the furthest apart from similar titles.

The type of game that doesn't direct you to its every corner in pursuit of some type of reward or checklist is few and far between, especially when you're talking about sprawling, open-world RPGs. The Witcher 3 and Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom come to mind, the latter in particular far more interested in getting you to play around with its tools than simply achieving set goals. But certainly there's been a trend of open world games that do the opposite - Assassin's Creed titles have long leaned towards completing tasks and collecting items. And in fact, Grand Theft Auto itself used to ask much more of the player in terms of collectibles and minigames if anyone wanted to attempt to 100% them. The likes of Vice City Stories and Liberty City Stories were much smaller games, but searching for red balloons and stray pigeons was something of a drag towards the end of the PS2 era. That GTA 6 is so deliberately shrugging that off is what could turn it into the next great open-world benchmark.

#3811. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

I hate to disagree with the legend on this one, but this feels pretentious.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If there was a Mt. Rushmore for hosts of food television shows, Gordon Ramsay is up there zero questions. As such, I tend to respect the things he says when it comes to the food world, but now I'm questioning the legend. This guy hates air fryers, and I can't help but feel he's being a bit pretentious.

The legendary chef and television host sat down with Variety to talk about a wide variety of topics. The subject turned to the air fryer, and I was shocked to hear that Ramsay is passionately opposed to them. Allegedly, he's even allergic to them:

I’m allergic to them. I break out in a severe fucking rash. You can’t get decent color in an air fryer. No color, no flavor...Jesus Christ! I developed the most amazing hybrid technology non-stick pan.

I was willing to defend Ramsay after he dissed pineapple on pizza, as that's a pretty standard opinion to have. I even continue to tune into his shows, despite them largely feeling like the same show as the last one, with a slightly different name.

I Had No Idea Gordon Ramsay And Tom Holland Knew One Another And Took The Same Flight For Months

What I can't abide is the disrespect he showed toward the air fryer. His comments make it sound like it has no place in the standard home kitchen. As someone who cooks from home all the time, I can't praise the air fryer enough, and how it elevates my cooking experience each and every dinner night.

As someone who is obsessed with Gordon Ramsay's shows, I understand he holds every chef, regardless of establishment, to a high standard. He wants them to know the ins and outs of cooking, how to perfectly pan-fry meats and what have you. On an ideal night, I'd love to prepare a meal with the best techniques and execute the perfect dish for my loved ones.

The reality is, life gets busy. Sometimes you work late, the kids have activities, or you're jet-setting across the world with Tom Holland. The air fryer is a time-saving kitchen device that allows me to pop something in there and not have to keep as close of an eye on it as I might in the pan.

It can also double as a smaller oven, for those ambitious enough to prepare multiple things for dinner and step away from the litany of one-pan wonders that can be served up. Juggling multiple things may be a snap for a classically trained chef, but for us amateurs, it's when mistakes can happen.

The air fryer promises consistency and, when used in the right context, can be a sous chef for the common man. I think the debate on this device's relevance in the home kitchen ended a while ago, but I fear Gordon Ramsay just reignited it with his hot take.

To which I will say, Gordon knows what restaurants are doing wrong, but I trust him less when it comes to speaking on personal kitchens. There's a lot I love about Ramsay, but this one I have to say he's wrong on. I'll still watch his shows, and hey, maybe he'll soften his stance as time passes and start to see the value in air fryers as I do.

#3808. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more."

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

#3807. Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

It's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

"We anticipate having more information to share come January."

Rolling dice over Thanksgiving doesn't have to be dull, as these highly recommended board games prove. Want to avoid another family get-together battling over Bond Street in Monopoly? There are five beginner-friendly must-haves I'll always recommend for families, and these up the ante without overcomplicating things.

Actually, these are often called 'gateway' games; they're ideal for newcomers and folks who don't have much experience beyond staples like Clue. Easy to learn but with enough nuance to keep you coming back for more, the five highly recommended board games I've listed below are a step up from old favorites yet don't feel overwhelming. They're not just for beginners, either. Some have reshaped the face of the industry with trend-setting mechanics, and I'd say they deserve a place amongst the very best board games.

Looking for something very straightforward? This is where I'd start. As noted in our Carcassonne review, the tile-laying game is "inoffensive family fun with heaps of replayability." Basically, you're building a patchwork kingdom and are trying to claim certain landmarks like cities or roads to earn points. Because you have a limited number of tokens to put on the board (and they stay there until those landmarks are finished), being flexible and knowing when to cut your losses is key.

If your family isn't up for anything complicated, this is my go-to recommendation. Herd Mentality is an easy-going and thoroughly silly board game about not standing out (which makes it great for those who hate the spotlight). You're all asked a simple question like "what is the best sauce?" and then have to scribble down an answer based on what you think everyone else will say. So long as you're in the majority, you get a point. That makes it a great warmup game or a decent choice if everyone's tired and sluggish after Thanksgiving dinner.

This may be the ultimate party game for many, but it's also a great choice for family get-togethers; as we say in our five-star Codenames review, it's the "ultimate pick-up-and-play party game." After splitting off into teams, you've got to track down specific words laid out in a grid if you want to win - but the team-member guiding you can only provide a single clue that connects them. It's a lot of fun and real headscratcher for everyone involved.

Want something that's still easy-going but is more advanced? I'll always go to bat for this modern classic. Your aim's to complete train routes across North America for points, but there are limited tracks. That means you'll have to judge where your opponents want to go and cut them off at the pass, or risk having to go the long way around and waste precious time. Like I say in my Ticket to Ride review, it feels like a satisfying puzzle with a layer of strategy underneath it all.

It's not exaggerating to say that this is one of the most influential board games of the past 30 years, and it's had an immense impact on the hobby. This is a very clever strategy game about settling an uninhabited island with multiple ways to win, and while it's the most tactical option on this list, it's arguably the best - part of the reason we gave it such a glowing writeup in our Catan review is that you can keep coming back without having the same outcome.

#3805. The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the big deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

This is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

#3804. GTA 6 leaker claims to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of Rockstar's crimsim onto the net, shouts that the "community will have it emulated inside a week"

Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.

"It is done," a statement posted on Cyberleek’s website claimed. "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one - the main executable - held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

So, more anime villain chatter from Cyberleek, who claim the executable file is on a timer and will be released immediately if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. It looks like the build is yet to be confirmed as genuine.

If any build leak were to result in GTA 6 being emulated on PC in rapid fashion, that would threaten to undercut an official port. Rockstar have yet to confirm that such a port is on the way and when it'll drop, but an October report from GamesBeat claimed the first three months of 2027 as the window in which Rockstar plan to deliver the game to PC. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij recently told our Edwin he reckons that concerns about unofficial ports based on the console version of GTA 6, likely made with generative AI, might lead Rockstar not to leave too big a gap before bringing the crimsim to PC officially.

Any alleged playable unofficial port of GTA 6 made with help from genAI and chucked online could, of course, just be a great big pile of malware.

Rockstar, who previously called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking", as well as parent company Take-Two, looked to have begun a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August.

You remember when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake launched earlier this month on Nintendo Switch 2, and it was running on PC in hours? Well, modders are claiming essentially the same will be happening for Grand Theft Auto 6, a much bigger and more complicated game.

If you're wondering how these games are getting ported so quickly, it's a mixture of people dumping the game files for the public to access and, oftentimes, generative AI coding doing a lot of the grunt work of recompiling.

Just yesterday, Cyberleek (the hacking team or person who leaked GTA 6 files earlier this year) reportedly leaked the GTA 6 Xbox build, giving modders access to the game's release files. That's one important part of the porting process checked off.

The only file Cyberleek says it hasn't dropped is the main executable file, and they say they will release it when their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. However, Cyberleek did say they would drop the exe file on November 23 either way. Even Cyberleek claims "this community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps"

Game modder OptiJuegos notes that GTA 6 is a GDK App, sharing its architecture with Windows and hoped for a dump of the Xbox version just a few days ago so it would run easily on PC, before Cyberleek's dump of the Xbox version.

Por suerte GTA 6 es una APP GDK y comparte casi toda la arquitectura con WindowsEsperemos algun DUMP de la version de XBOX. No hay nada publico en los servidores pic.twitter.com/8V0u3FHXSANovember 18, 2026

Cybersecurity expert VX Underground took a look at the Xbox file dump and reckons it's real, and even reckons it will be playable on the 23rd if the executable file is released. Another X user notes that the dump appears to be missing the "EmbeddedXvd folders that is inside the gameos.xvd" which apparently contain system DLL files, as well as the NT kernel and drivers. Still, this is something modders can work around.

> wake up> take a shit> get out of bed> check beep boop> over 9000 DMs> "SCHMEELI, GTA VI LEAK"> ???> sends link> torrent> ok> look inside> actual assets> huh> squint eyes> look closer> not larphuh, how about that. the cyberleek guy released the full xbox gta 6… pic.twitter.com/1MDrGI97DyNovember 19, 2026

There's nothing to do but wait to see if modders actually will release a port of GTA 6 on PC, but Rockstar is infamously litigious, and emulation is a legally grey area at best, and downright illegal at worst. Emulation tools and recompilers aren't illegal by themselves, but downloading ROMs and game dumps you don't own is a form of copyright infringement, and game companies would argue that it costs them a lot of cash at the end of the day.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

If you're planning on waiting and playing the game legally when it eventually launches on PC, that lead time for modders does mean the GTA 6 modding scene will likely be seriously vibrant by launch, though.

3. Best handheld gaming PC: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X

4. Best mini PC: Minisforum AtomMan G7 PT

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

What do Disney Parks, Make-A-Wish, and the Hallmark Channel all have in common? They love making dreams come true, and that’s exactly what happened for one teenage Hallmark movie superfan who has dreamt about being in one of the cable channel’s movies for a very long time.

Make-A-Wish partnered with Hallmark and Disney to make 14-year-old Ceci’s dreams come true, flying her and her family out to Disney World in Orlando, Florida, to appear in the upcoming Hallmark movie set at a Disney Park. Just like the film’s star Lacey Chabert, Ceci’s day started in the hair and makeup chair as the dedicated artists prepped her for a big moment. She was then decked out in new Christmas Disney Parks merch by wardrobe before being taken to set, where she not only got her own chair with her name on it, but also got a chance to meet with the cast of the highly anticipated Hallmark holiday flick.

Both Ceci and her mom got to appear in what is apparently one of the major scenes in the holiday romance film, titled Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True. They can be seen as hotel guests, sitting in the lobby of Disney’s Polynesian Village Resort holding Minnie Mouse and Dumbo plushies. I know I’m definitely going to be keeping my eyes open for the mother-daughter duo when the movie premieres as part of the 2026 TV Schedule on the Hallmark Channel on November 28th at 8 p.m. ET.

The excitement didn’t stop there, though, because Ceci also got a chance to step behind the camera alongside the film’s director. Not only did she get to learn what goes into directing one of Hallmark’s biggest movies yet, but she also got to yell “Action” on set. Watch:

A post shared by Disney Parks (@disneyparks)

Filming wrapped early this year on what could be Hallmark’s best Countdown to Christmas movie of 2026, but the magic hasn’t stopped for Ceci, who was surprised once again when her entire family was flown back out to Walt Disney World to attend the red-carpet premiere.

As if walking a red carpet as a teenager isn’t exciting enough, she also got to pose alongside the film’s star. I don’t know what I’m more jealous of: the fact that she got to walk the red carpet or that she got to see Chabert in her stunning Disney Princess-inspired gown. Probably both! Ceci stunned as well in a gorgeous burgundy gown that is perfect for the holiday season.

All of this is making me more excited for the film! Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True centers on Lindsey (Chabert), who plans to spend the holidays at Disney World with her extended family. In addition to having the best holiday ever, Lindsey also makes a wish at Cinderella’s Fountain for a love worthy of a fairytale to find her.

Enter Philip (Travis Van Winkle), a man Lindsey went on a disastrous first date with who just so happens to also be spending the holiday with his family at the “Most Magical Place On Earth.” As Lindsey and Philip’s paths continue to cross, sparks start to fly. It seems like Ceci isn’t the only one whose wish is going to be coming true.

Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True premieres first on the Hallmark Channel on November 28th, but will be available to stream the next day on Hallmark+ and Disney+ with an active subscription.

#3801. GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

"The decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers."

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop."

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition."

Though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3800. Amid a year of layoffs, Ubisoft yank the cover off Motherbrain, their new studio "focused on AI for gameplay innovation"

Something something "proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators" something something

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

You'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months."

That'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

You can fly a GTA 6 jet right at the start of the game by raiding the nearby military base, and here's how to do it

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Knowing how to get a jet in GTA 6 is essential information if you're planning to cause chaos, as taking control of one of these military aircraft is considered peak criminal behavior. While you'd expect that significant progress in GTA 6 would be required before you even had a chance of swiping such high-end hardware, you can actually go and help yourself to one pretty much as soon as you start the game. To try it yourself, here's how to steal a jet in GTA 6.

The location for a number of GTA 6 jets is the Mile Zero Air Station, which is found by heading west along the main road from the starting area, through Abismo Key, then on to Southwind and the miliary base itself.

You can drive there in any vehicle, though I recommend not using your GTA 6 personal vehicle as it will get trashed and left inside the base, so steal a sturdy and reasonably fast vehicle for the job. Purchasing and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation will also improve your odds of surviving the initial stage.

Follow the route marked on my map above, which will lead you through some barriers on the road to a set of soldiers who will open fire, then take the first turning right and drive through more soldiers until you see a dirt pile ahead that you can hit to clear the security fences. This is also a Stunt Jump, though you don't need to complete it as long as you clear the perimeter and land on the runway.

Once on the runway inside the miliary base, drive straight ahead to where you'll see several GTA 6 jets parked up next to hangars. Pull up alongside one, jump out of your car and hop straight into the cockpit, before firing up the afterburner and turning onto the runway to take off.

Once you've taken control of your jet and got airborne, follow the prompt to retract the landing gear and you're away! Be aware that you'll have attracted at least a five-star GTA 6 Wanted Level with this theft, which could go up to six if you start blowing things up, so multiple military jets will be scrambled to shoot you down with homing missiles. I was barely able to reach the first bridge before getting blown out of the sky, but if you fly low and take evasive action you may fare better – good luck!

If you're looking for an impressive ride that's easier to obtain then here's how to steal the GTA 6 Paul Walker car, which you can then use to arrive in style at the various GTA 6 Strip Club locations around Leonida.
